text:
marta.k: quick heads-up — i opened a terraform PR to switch our model configmap templating to a per-model overrides map. want to make sure this won’t unexpectedly roll all model pods in prod. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pull/842 :eyes:

alex.c: can you paste the exact terraform change? is it changing the configmap name or just keys inside it?

marta.k: it only changes how we render the data keys, we add a new var called `model_config_overrides` which is a map(string) keyed by model id. snippet from the tf module:

```hcl
resource "kubernetes_config_map" "model_cfg" {
  metadata {
    name = "model-${var.model_id}-cfg"
    annotations = {
      "redwood.com/config-hash" = sha256(join("\n", values(local.rendered_data)))
    }
  }
  data = local.rendered_data
}

locals {
  rendered_data = merge(var.base_config, var.model_config_overrides[var.model_id] != null ? var.model_config_overrides[var.model_id] : {})
}
```

liam.s: good call adding `config-hash` annotation — our model controller watches that annotation for restarts. if TF sets it deterministically from the merged map it'll only restart when content actually changes. just confirm ordering is stable (you're using `values()` — that can be nondeterministic).

marta.k: ah good catch — i copied quick example. i'm going to replace `values()` with a sorted join, e.g. `join("|", sort(keys(local.rendered_data)))` + jsonencode for values before hashing.

alex.c: also check if the controller expects certain top-level keys (like `feature_flags` vs `flags`). some older models read `flags` directly from the configmap and will ignore renamed fields. migrating keys could be a silent break.

marta.k: i ran a grep across model repos — most expect `feature_flags` but 2 older training-models expect `flags`. plan is to keep both for a transition window.

eng-sre-bot: FYI — if this change touches the configmap name pattern we’ll need to update the serviceaccount roles in the TF module. current RBAC assumes `model-*-cfg`.

liam.s: can we avoid dual-key duplication by creating a small compatibility layer in the controller that maps `feature_flags` -> `flags` for legacy models? less churn on infra.

marta.k: makes sense. i’ll open a tiny controller PR for a fallback mapping and add a staging smoke test.

alex.c: what about secrets? will this PR touch the secret sync tooling that mirrors KMS-managed secrets into the namespace?

marta.k: no secret schema change, but the operator will read `secretsRef` from the configmap data for a couple models. i verified the referenced secret names are unchanged.

ops-bot: terraform plan for `modules/model-config` in staging completed: no plan diffs that modify resource names.

liam.s: cool. can we do a canary rollout — apply to staging first, then prod-canary (one model pool) and SRE will monitor latency/error spikes? @eng-sre-bot can you watch? :mag: 

eng-sre-bot: acknowledged. i’ll add a short monitor for pod restarts, 95p latency, and 5xx spikes during the canary window.

marta.k: thanks all. i’ll update TF to use sorted keys for the hash, add controller fallback mapping, and re-request review. pinging @alex.c and @liam.s for quick PR review before i merge (aiming EOD). :thumbsup:
